For a fully amortized loan, the monthly payment is

\[
\text{PMT}=P\frac{r(1+r)^n}{(1+r)^n-1},
\qquad
\text{Total cost}=n(\text{PMT})-P+\text{fee}
\]

where \(P=\$50{,}000\) and \(r=\text{APR}/12\).

**Loan A:** \(r=0.059/12=0.0049167,\ n=48\)

\[
\text{PMT}\approx \$1{,}171.96
\]
\[
\text{Interest}=48(1{,}171.96)-50{,}000\approx \$6{,}254.10
\]
Fee \(=\$0\), so total cost \(\approx \$6{,}254.10\).

**Loan B:** \(r=0.069/12=0.00575,\ n=48\)

\[
\text{PMT}\approx \$1{,}194.99
\]
\[
\text{Interest}=48(1{,}194.99)-50{,}000\approx \$7{,}359.70
\]
Fee \(=3\%\times 50{,}000=\$1{,}500\), so total cost \(\approx \$8{,}859.70\).

**Loan C:** \(r=0.059/12=0.0049167,\ n=36\)

\[
\text{PMT}\approx \$1{,}518.83
\]
\[
\text{Interest}=36(1{,}518.83)-50{,}000\approx \$4{,}677.97
\]
Fee \(=1\%\times 50{,}000=\$500\), so total cost \(\approx \$5{,}177.97\).

Loan C has the lowest total cost.
